title: Choose Decraft's visual direction
question: Which direction should carry the landing page's story and the app's responsive design?

options.label: The open market lane
options.lineage: Nigerian market passages and working-street wayfinding
options.thesis: A familiar street of makers becomes a route into the work behind each name.
options.viewport: A working signboard introduces Decraft, then opens into one maker's project story with direct routes to discovery and portfolio creation.
options.risk: The street could read as a marketplace before the project archive is clear.

raised.raise: Each artisan keeps a distinct identity without implying credentials Decraft has not verified.
Craft-forward display type is paired with highly legible interface typography.

options.label: The project folio
options.lineage: A maker's portfolio folio: one record per project, opened to show its evidence and progress.
options.thesis: Each project opens as a readable work record, then joins a portfolio customers can explore.
options.viewport: One generous project folio pairs a strong work image with the story, milestones, and a visible route to browse or create a portfolio.
options.risk: Editorial folios are familiar; the live progress sequence must distinguish this from a static gallery.

raised.raise: Keep maker and project history attached to every piece of evidence.
Make browse-by-location a clear customer action rather than a decorative nav link.

options.label: The work quilt
options.lineage: Hand-pieced cloth carrying dates and personal histories.
options.thesis: Project fragments join into a record with a visible maker and history.
options.viewport: Unequal project fragments form a patchwork record with maker, date, and progress kept visible.
options.case: Competitive: craft lineage resonates, but textile imagery can narrow a platform for many trades.
options.risk: A textile-led identity may imply Decraft is only for fabric crafts.

options.label: The project through time
options.lineage: An architectural section showing spaces and their changing use through the day.
options.thesis: A project's progress becomes a legible sequence rather than a single after-photo.
options.viewport: A project image anchors a chronological strip of preparation, work in progress, and completion.
options.case: Competitive: time-based reading clarifies the timeline, though daylight itself is not true of every craft.
options.risk: The building-specific metaphor could crowd out non-construction trades.

options.label: The maker league
options.lineage: A fictional racing identity built from livery, velocity, and team marks.
options.thesis: Every maker's work is a bold mark moving through a high-energy directory.
options.viewport: A fast, high-contrast page frames makers as a roster and projects as featured entries.
options.case: Declined: racing-team competition does not match the practical, trust-first job or explain project evidence.
options.kept: A maker's identity should be recognizable across their profile and projects.
options.risk: The league metaphor may imply rankings and competitive status.

options.label: The maker's rack
options.lineage: A skate-shop wall where each deck carries an artist's own image and mark.
options.thesis: Let the finished work lead, with every project carrying its maker's character.
options.viewport: Tall project panels stand like objects on a rack, each led by its strongest work example.
options.case: Competitive: maker-led objects resonate, but the skate-specific form is too narrow for the platform.
options.risk: A youth-culture deck wall may misrepresent other trades and customers.

options.label: The type workshop
options.lineage: An interactive type specimen where glyphs shift along a live design axis.
options.thesis: Craft is expressed through an unusually considered typographic voice.
options.viewport: A giant type form introduces a brief message, with the page’s craft expressed through precise type scale.
options.case: Declined: typography alone neither identifies the artisan audience nor explains the project-to-portfolio mechanism.
options.kept: Display typography can carry personality while interface copy stays clear and readable.
options.risk: A font-demo interaction would distract from real work.

options.label: The local work board
options.lineage: A public departure board with fixed columns and changing destinations.
options.thesis: A clear, changing directory helps customers orient themselves quickly.
options.viewport: Rows pair craft, project, and area so visitors can scan relevant makers.
options.case: Competitive: scannable location and service summaries help discovery, but a board alone does not tell the work story.
options.risk: A transport-board metaphor can make artisans look like listings instead of people with portfolios.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A generic SaaS landing page with a centered headline, feature cards, and one signup button.
canonCard.viewport: A centered hero and three equal feature cards explain the product in a familiar software template.
canonCard.risk: This may be immediately legible but indistinguishable from other platforms.
